args.text: [lane-lynx] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System, the internet's address book) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: users are sent to servers that have moved or been retired, causing failures. (2) Slow recovery: when you switch traffic during an outage, old answers keep pointing at the broken place until they expire. (3) Lingering bad data: a poisoned or hijacked answer stays in the cache for longer, so harm lasts longer.

[lane-lynx] Idempotent retries matter because networks fail in ways that leave you unsure whether a request worked, so you must be able to send it again safely. An idempotent request gives the same result however many times it runs, so a retry cannot cause double charges, duplicate orders or other repeated side effects.

[lane-lynx] Two trade-offs of using UUIDv7 (version 7 of the Universally Unique Identifier) as a primary key: (1) Size: it takes 16 bytes, which is bigger than a plain whole-number key, so tables and indexes use more storage and memory. (2) Leaked timing: the first part holds the creation time, so anyone who sees an identifier can work out roughly when the record was made, and records created in the same millisecond are not strictly ordered unless extra care is taken.

[lane-lynx] A write-ahead log (WAL) is a file where a database records each change before it alters the main data, so nothing is lost if the system crashes part-way. After a crash, the database replays the log to restore a consistent state, and the log also gives a quick, sequential way to write changes safely to disk.

[lane-lynx] Two reasons to pin a client version in a benchmark: (1) Fair comparison: a newer client may change speed, retry behaviour or default settings, so results from different runs would no longer be measuring the same thing. (2) Repeatability: anyone can rerun the test later and get comparable figures, and any change in results can be traced to the system under test rather than to a silent client update.
